sections.h2: Where is Anderson, SC, and how did it start?
sections.html:
Anderson is the seat of Anderson County in the northwest corner of South Carolina, on the Piedmont plateau. It covers about 15.86 square miles and sits roughly midway along the I-85 corridor, about 120 miles from Atlanta and 140 miles from Charlotte.

Anderson District was formed in 1826, and the town took the name of Revolutionary War veteran Robert Anderson. It was called Anderson Court House until 1895. The "Electric City" nickname comes from a hydroelectric plant on the Rocky River that powered the town in the 1890s.

The 2020 Census counted 28,106 people in the city, up from 26,686 in 2010. That makes Anderson the smallest of the Upstate's three primary cities, but the county around it is far larger, with 203,718 residents in 2020. For a seller, the practical point is that the city and the county are different layers: City of Anderson taxes are collected at the county's offices, so the county Treasurer is the office to call.

sections.h2: What drives the economy around Anderson?
sections.html:
Manufacturing is the largest source of jobs in Anderson County, about 22.7 percent of employment, followed by health care at 15.7 percent and retail at 13.2 percent. The county reports more than 230 manufacturers, 22 of them international, in automotive products, metal products, industrial machinery, plastics, publishing and textiles.

Named county employers include AnMed Health Medical Center, Anderson University, Bosch, the City of Anderson, Glen Raven, Ingles, Michelin, Walmart and Walgreens. Anderson University has roughly 3,900 students, and Tri-County Technical College and Carolina Bible College also have a presence in the area.

  • Hospital, university and plant employers are all inside the county.
  • I-85 links the city to Greenville and the wider Upstate job market.
  • The Greenville-Anderson-Greer metro area had about 975,480 residents in 2023.

Where your house sits in relation to those employers and exits is worth mentioning when you describe it to any buyer.

sections.h2: What do schools, roads and weather mean for an Anderson house?
sections.html:
Anderson School District Five serves the city, with Westside High and T. L. Hanna High as its two high schools. District boundaries matter to buyers, so confirm the address with the district before you list anything about schools.

I-85 is the only freeway through the city, with five signed exits. Other routes include US 29, US 76, US 178 and SC 187. Anderson Regional Airport is about three miles away, and the nearest commercial airport is Greenville-Spartanburg International, about 42 miles away. There are six local bus routes running hourly, plus Clemson Area Transit's 4U route.

Weather is mild and wet. Federal 1991 to 2020 normals put the July average high near 90.7 degrees and the January average high near 53.2 degrees, with about 50 inches of precipitation spread through the year and almost no snow. Heat and steady rain mostly show up in roofs, gutters, crawl space moisture and air conditioning age, which are the items inspectors and buyers look at first.

sections.h2: Who sends Anderson property tax bills, and when are they due?
sections.html:
City of Anderson property taxes are due on or before January 15, and they are paid at the Anderson County Annex, 401 East River Street. The city's own tax page says a 15 percent penalty applies after January 15 and refers questions to the Anderson County Treasurer at (864) 260-4033.

The county Treasurer says notices go out on October 1, and the payment is due in full by January 15 of the following year. Penalties accrue on January 16, February 2 and March 17. South Carolina law sets those steps at 3 percent, then 7 percent more, then 5 percent more, which adds up to the 15 percent the city mentions. After March 17 the treasurer can issue a tax execution for the taxes, penalties and costs.

You can pay in person in Anderson or Powdersville, by mail with a check, or online. Card payments carry a convenience fee on the Treasurer's page. If a mortgage company pays your bill from escrow, forward the notice to the lender.

sections.h2: How is an Anderson house assessed, and how do you appeal?
sections.html:
Anderson County taxes a legal residence at a 4 percent assessment ratio and most other real property at 6 percent. The 4 percent rate is not automatic. The assessor says to apply as soon as you move in, and the window runs through January 15, when taxes are due. Second homes, vacation homes and rentals do not qualify.

If you disagree with a value, the assessor's page describes this path:

  • Send a written objection within 90 days of the assessment notice, with your estimate of market value and supporting documents.
  • After the assessor responds, you have 30 days to appeal to the Board of Assessment Appeals.
  • After the board decides, you have 30 days to request a contested case hearing at the Administrative Law Court.
  • If nothing is resolved by December 31, you can ask in writing for a bill at 80 percent of the protested value.

An appeal does not pause the due date, and penalties are not waived for paying late. The county's appeal form also asks for one form per parcel, and it will not process unsigned or unsupported forms.

sections.h2: What happens to the value when an Anderson house sells?
sections.html:
Most sales are an assessable transfer of interest, and the new owner's value is reset to full market value without the 15 percent cap. The assessor explains that transferred property is assessed at full fair market value in the year after the transfer. State law lists deeds, trust conveyances and distributions under a will among the transfers that count, with exceptions for things like certain family transfers and foreclosures before the redemption period ends.

The buyer must also apply for the 4 percent rate on a home they will occupy. For a 6 percent transfer, the county has a 25 percent ATI exemption form, due January 30 of the following year.

For you as the seller, this mostly affects what the buyer will pay next year. Your own bill for the year of sale is still based on the value that was on the roll.

sections.h2: What if the Anderson taxes are already unpaid?
sections.html:
Once the penalty steps run, the county can sell the property at a delinquent tax sale. The owner, a grantee, or a mortgage or judgment creditor can redeem within twelve months by paying the taxes, penalties and costs plus interest on the bid amount. That interest steps up by quarter, from 3 percent to 12 percent.

Selling before a tax sale lets the closing agent pay the back taxes from your proceeds. If the title changed during the year and the new owner never received a notice, state law tells the treasurer to waive the penalties.

  • Ask the Treasurer for a payoff figure good through your closing date.
  • Ask the closing attorney how the current year's bill will be split.
  • Confirm whether any rollback tax applies if the land was farmed.

The county assessor notes that buyer and seller decide at closing who pays rollback taxes on agricultural land.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale work with tax due on an Anderson house?
sections.html:
A cash buyer pays off the tax at closing from the sale price, so you do not need to bring money to the table. You send the closing attorney your latest bill and any past-due notices, and the attorney orders the payoff from the Anderson County Treasurer.

Cash Home Buyers buys houses in Anderson as they are, including houses with deferred repairs, tenants or inherited title. Tell us about the property, the amount owed and your timing, and we will tell you plainly whether we can make an offer.

faqs.q: When are Anderson, SC property taxes due?
faqs.a: They are due on or before January 15. Anderson County mails notices on October 1, and the city's page says a 15 percent penalty applies after January 15.

faqs.q: Where do I pay City of Anderson property tax?
faqs.a: The city's page says to pay at the Anderson County Annex, 401 East River Street. The Treasurer also takes payments in Powdersville, by mail, and online, and you can call (864) 260-4033.

faqs.q: Do I get the 4 percent rate automatically after buying in Anderson?
faqs.a: No. The buyer files a legal residence application with the county assessor, and the county says to do so as soon as you move in. The window runs through January 15.

faqs.q: How long do I have to dispute an Anderson assessment?
faqs.a: You have 90 days from the assessment notice to object in writing. If no notice was mailed, an appeal received before January 15 applies to that tax year.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Anderson house that has delinquent taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The closing agent pays the back taxes, penalties and costs from the proceeds. Get a payoff figure from the Treasurer so the closing date and the amount match.

faqs.q: What is the redemption period after a tax sale in South Carolina?
faqs.a: It is twelve months from the sale date. The owner pays the taxes, penalties and costs plus interest that runs from 3 percent in the first quarter to 12 percent in the last.
